title: multipart: enforce file payload limits and content-type validation for OpenAI-compat /files API
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Enforce multipart file size limits and content-type validation for the OpenAI-compatible /files endpoint; return clear HTTP errors and add metrics.
description:
Motivation: The OpenAI-compat /files multipart upload path was too permissive: large binary uploads and ambiguous content types caused worker OOMs and downstream inference failures in private deployments. This PR implements server-side enforcement for file payload size and explicit content-type validation to improve stability and provide clearer errors for clients.

What I changed: added a multipart validator middleware that checks Content-Type headers, enforces per-file and total multipart body size limits, and normalizes OpenAI-compat error responses. Updated the OpenAI compatibility shim so requests routed through the /v1/files endpoint get the same validation semantics as Redwood's native endpoints. Also added integration tests and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Add middleware that enforces per-file max_size and aggregate max_body_size (configurable via env/flags)
- [x] Content-Type whitelist for text/*, application/json, application/octet-stream, image/*, audio/*; unknown types return 422
- [x] Return 413 for payloads exceeding limits with structured OpenAI-compatible error body
- [x] Instrument metrics for rejected uploads (content_type_rejects, size_rejects)
- [x] Update Python SDK compatibility shim to bubble-up 413/422 errors with helpful messages
- [x] Docs: document limits and recommended client behavior

Backward compatibility: This is intentionally conservative. Existing clients that previously uploaded large files will now receive 413 and must retry with a smaller file or use the Private installer to raise limits. Error codes and bodies were aligned with OpenAI-compat expectations so most SDKs can handle them without code changes.

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests were added. In CI one integration job hit a timeout on the first run (flaky e2e under heavy load) and was retried; final CI status is green. We will feature-flag the stricter validation for a gradual rollout to Dedicated and Private clusters during the next two weeks.

Notes for operators: New config knobs: FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_PER_FILE_BYTES and FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES. Default values chosen to be safe for hosted tier (50MB per file, 200MB total). Private/Dedicated customers can adjust via config or installer. Metrics: file_upload_size_rejected_total, file_upload_content_type_rejected_total.

Related: ENG-4021 (stability), ENG-4045 (openai-compat feature parity).

api: enforce per-file and total multipart size limits
compat: OpenAI shim normalize error responses (413/422)
sdk/python: raise informative exceptions for 413/422 on file uploads
tests: integration coverage for multipart size and content-type validation
docs: add file upload limits and recovery guidance
diff_snippets:
--- a/server/middleware/multipart_validator.go
+++ b/server/middleware/multipart_validator.go
@@
-// previous naive stream handling
+// validate multipart streams early to avoid OOMs
+if file.Size > cfg.MaxPerFileBytes {
+  return httpError(413, "file too large")
+}

--- a/server/api/openai_compat/files_handler.go
+++ b/server/api/openai_compat/files_handler.go
@@
-// previously accepted any content-type
+ct := req.Header.Get("Content-Type")
+if !isAllowedContentType(ct) {
+  return writeOpenAIError(w, 422, "unsupported content type")
+}
reviews: Connor Liu: Left a couple of small nits around config naming (FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_PER_FILE_BYTES vs FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_FILE_BYTES) — prefer explicit 'per_file' wording. Also questioned the default 50MB value; sounds reasonable for hosted but callout needed in docs.
Aisha Patel (author): Responded: switched to FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_PER_FILE_BYTES and added note in docs. Kept 50MB default after discussion with infra — it's consistent with current object-store limits.
Mariana Gomez: Approve after minor docs tweak. Suggested emitting a 'file.upload.accepted' event for downstream ingestion pipelines — added a lightweight metric and event hook.
Evan Park: Verified tests and load-run in staging; recommended a progressive rollout to Dedicated clusters. Approved.

notes_on_backcompat: Clients that relied on unconstrained uploads will see 413/422; documented guidance recommends chunking or using alternate hosting for large assets. No changes to tokenization or inference paths.
